timelineSection.title: A New Generation of Faith in Asia
timelineSection.subtitle: OUR JOURNEY (2022 - 2026)

detail.theme: "Winds of Change — The Future Church of Asia"
detail.tagline: Reconnecting Asia's Church Networks After the Pandemic
paragraphs: As the world was still in its post-pandemic recovery, churches across Asia faced the challenges of suspended gatherings, restricted cross-border exchanges, and shifting mission models. The 1st IAA Summit convened in Kuala Lumpur, becoming one of the few representative transnational in-person gatherings of Asian churches in the post-pandemic era.

The assembly centered on the core vision of "Mutual Flourishing, Mutual Learning, Mutual Sharing," emphasizing the need for closer cooperation among Asian churches to break through the limitations of independent development. Pastors, missionaries, and marketplace leaders from various nations and cities gathered to engage in deep dialogue — from how churches responded during the pandemic to the role of Asian evangelical work in the future.

This inaugural gathering put forward a pivotal idea: Asian churches are not merely recipients of resources, but should gradually become exporters of Gospel mission and influence. IAA began building its foundation as a transnational connecting platform, laying the groundwork for future regional collaboration across Asia.

detail.tagline: Finding the Possibility of Faith and Vocation Walking Together in a Changing Era
paragraphs: The 2nd IAA Summit moved to Jakarta. As a major commercial and economic center in Southeast Asia, Jakarta symbolizes rapid change and intense challenge — echoing this edition's theme of "Walking on Waves".

That year, the assembly placed greater focus on the connection between the marketplace, the city, and faith. Participants included not only church leaders, but also business owners, young entrepreneurs, and cross-sector professionals, exploring topics such as digital transformation, urban renewal, workplace mission, and cross-cultural collaboration.

Through forums and on-site visits, participants from different nations were able to build exchanges and partnerships in real cultural settings. IAA also began to take on a distinctive identity in this edition — not only focused on internal church development, but on how faith can enter society, industries, and the public sphere to respond to Asia's rapidly changing context.

detail.tagline: Exploring Deeper Transformation Amid Geopolitical Shifts and the AI Wave
paragraphs: The 3rd IAA Summit returned to Kaohsiung, Taiwan. As a major port city in southern Taiwan, Kaohsiung has long carried a history of mission, industry, and international exchange — making it a meaningful symbol for this year's gathering.

Facing rapid global shifts and the new challenges brought by AI technology, the assembly adopted the theme of "Launch Out Into the Deep," encouraging Asian churches and Christian leaders to move beyond surface-level connections and engage more deeply with questions of cultural, professional, and systemic transformation.

This year's forums covered topics including tech ethics, sustainable governance (ESG), media influence, and cross-generational leadership, drawing leaders from diverse industries and nations. IAA also began to more clearly focus on a key question: "In an era of rising global uncertainty, how can Asian churches build resilient cooperative networks and meaningful public influence?"

detail.tagline: Seeing a New Beginning of Transnational Unity in Hard Gospel Soil
paragraphs: The 4th IAA Summit moved to Tokyo, held at Yodobashi Church. Japan has long been regarded as one of the most challenging regions for missions in Asia, making this summit a significant cross-cultural undertaking for IAA.

Church and marketplace leaders from Taiwan, Japan, the United States, Malaysia, Indonesia, South Korea, and Hong Kong gathered in Tokyo, forging deeper partnerships through worship, forums, and exchanges. Participants from different backgrounds, denominations, and generations engaged in more practical dialogue and fellowship on a shared platform.

Compared to previous summits that emphasized regional connectivity, this gathering placed greater stress on "unity" and "shared responsibility." In a city as highly modern yet deeply lonely as Tokyo, IAA sought to answer how Asian churches can bridge cultural and linguistic divides to face the challenges of the next generation together.
